## What this module is, and what it is not

Technical-analysis indicators over caller slices, numerically faithful to TA-Lib C 0.8.3: same
formulas, same order of floating-point operations, same constants, same parameter ranges and
lookbacks. Seed set: SMA, EMA, WMA, MA, MACD, MACDEXT, MACDFIX, RSI, BBANDS, TRANGE, ATR, NATR,
STOCH, STOCHF, MAX, MIN, SUM; wave I3: DEMA, TEMA, T3, TRIMA, KAMA, MIDPOINT, MIDPRICE, SAR, SAREXT, MAVP,
ACCBANDS, ALMA, CKSP, DONCHIAN, FRAMA, HMA, ICHIMOKU, KC, MCGD, RMA, SUPERTREND, SWAK_BUTTER, SWAK_GAUSS,
VIDYA, VWMA, ZIGZAG, ZLEMA. Every function has a batch form, a `Lookback` function and a
streaming type (MAVP excepted, see Limits; MACDEXT, STOCH, STOCHF, CKSP and ALMA additionally take an allocator first, used only for `f32` input or scratch, see Limits); the batch and streaming forms run the same core step, so they agree to the bit
(tested).

What a reader might expect and will not find: the other 196 TA-Lib functions (later waves, by
group), the candlestick patterns (planned in `src/candles.zig`), MAMA (and with it HT_TRENDLINE; they come
with the Cycle wave; `MaType.mama` answers `error.Unsupported`), TA-Lib's `startIdx`/`endIdx` range arguments (a batch call covers the whole slice;
`out[0..lookback]` is NaN), in-place calls (`out` must not alias `in`; TA-Lib allows it, see Backlog), and an abstract/function-table
interface.

## Wire format / algorithm

API (settled in `indicators-I2-design.md`): `fn <name>(comptime T: type, in, out…, params) Error!usize`
with `T` in {f32, f64} (the math is f64), `out.len == in.len` for every slice (else
`error.BadParam`), the first `lookback` slots NaN, the lookback returned. OHLC functions take
`high, low, close` slices of one length. `<name>Lookback(params) Error!usize`.

Cores (`src/core.zig`, `smooth.zig`): every indicator is a by-value `step(src, x) ?f64` core
counting the bars fed to it. A core that needs older values reads them through `src.at(i)`: a view
of the caller slice (batch) or a ring buffer (streaming). A composite feeds each component from the
bar where the component's own lookback ends exactly on the bar where the composite's does
(`skip = largest lookback - own lookback`, the way TA-Lib calls `TA_MA(startIdx = lookbackLargest …)`),
which fixes the seeding window of every SMA, WMA and EMA inside it.

Per-function notes from the C source (each read before it was ported):

- **EMA**: seed = SMA of the first `period` bars (MetaStock compatibility no longer exists in 0.8.x);
  `beta = (p-1)/(p+1)`, `k = 1-beta`, `beta` re-derived as `1-k` when `beta < 0.5`;
  `prev = fma(beta, prev, k*x)` (`@mulAdd`); period 1 is a copy (keeps -0.0). Lookback
  `p - 1 + unstable`; the stored unstable count applies even at period 1 (lookback = count).
  AUTO levels (period > 1): auto4 = (10p+1)/2, auto8 = (19p+1)/2.
- **SMA/SUM**: running sum, the bar leaves after the output is read (`out = sum / p`, then `sum -= oldest`).
- **WMA**: running weighted sum and plain sum, both rebuilt from the window (oldest first, weights
  1..p) every 8p outputs (the 0.8.x re-anchor); divider `p(p+1)/2` in double.
- **MA**: period 1 and `.disabled` are a copy with lookback 0 for every type; the SMA/EMA/WMA arms
  forward; every other type is `error.Unsupported`. Period range 1..100000, default 30.
- **MACD**: fast and slow are swapped when slow < fast; slow EMA from bar 0, fast from
  `Ls - Lf`, signal from the first line bar; first output at `Ls + Lg`. Signal period 1 copies the
  line, except that TA-Lib's very first signal value is `0.0 + line` (the SMA seed of one value); kept.
- **MACDEXT**: swaps periods and types; period range of fast/slow 2.., signal 1..; every component is
  an `ma` (any supported type); line values before the signal's first bar are not reported.
- **MACDFIX**: 12/26 with the fixed pair k = 0.15 / 0.075 (not 2/(p+1)), beta = 1-k, k = 1-beta, no
  `beta < 0.5` swap; the fast EMA runs as many unstable bars as the slow one.
- **RSI**: Wilder; one delta of lead, `p` deltas summed and divided for the seed; `100*g/(g+l)`, a
  window with neither gain nor loss answers 50 (0.8.x #480). Unstable lookback `p + u`, AUTO 10p / 19p.
- **TRANGE**: lookback 1 (bar 0 only supplies the previous close). **ATR**: seed = mean of the first
  `p` true ranges, then `fma(beta, atr, alpha*tr)` with `beta = (p-1)/p`, `alpha = 1-beta`; lookback
  `p + u`, AUTO `(10(2p-1)+1)/2` and `(19(2p-1)+1)/2`. **NATR**: the same recursion, AUTO 10p / 19p,
  output `atr / close * 100` of the bar's own close (a zero close answers 0), period 1 is the raw true range.
- **BBANDS**: the deviation is the population standard deviation of the window (TA_VAR with the
  shifted running sums and the re-anchor rules ported from `ta_VAR.c`), the middle band is any
  supported MA; period 2.., dev in [-3e37, 3e37]; `upper = mid + sd*up`, `lower = mid - sd*dn` (`fma` form
  when the two deviations differ). Lookback `max(MA lookback, p-1)`.
- **STOCH/STOCHF**: raw %K = 100*(C-LL)/(HH-LL), a window flat to within 1e-14 of its magnitude answers 0;
  %D/slow lines are MAs cascading on the previous stage; the first stage reports from the last stage's first bar.
- **MAX/MIN**: window extreme with index tracking and rescan on expiry (periods 2..); **SUM** period 2..

Wave I3 (each C function read before it was ported; same `step` cores, plus `src/hist.zig` for the
multi-input functions: a core reads the bar history through `h.at(i)` of a struct of f64 fields, outputs are
one slice per field):

- **DEMA / TEMA / T3** (`mavg.zig`, one `ChainCore`): K EMAs in lockstep, each seeded with the mean of its first `p`
  inputs. DEMA/TEMA start stage `j` at bar `j * L_ema` (every stage skips the unstable bars), lookback
  `K * L_ema`, EMA's beta/k pair; period 1 copies after `K * unstable` bars (the C comment: TA_MA reports 0, the
  function itself `K * unstable`, they disagree when the unstable period is non-zero; kept). T3 starts stage `j`
  at `j (p-1)` and adds the unstable bars at the end (lookback `6(p-1) + u`, AUTO `(11*8p+7)/8` / `(11*12p+7)/8`),
  uses `k = 2/(p+1)` and `1-k` without the beta swap, and the coefficients `c1..c4` of vfactor in `fma` form
  (`vfactor` in [0,1], default 0.7).
- **TRIMA**: the 0.8.x four-adjustment running numerator (odd and even period differ in the middle weight),
  period 1 is not a copy (`0.0 + x` seeds, so -0.0 becomes +0.0), as TA-Lib.
- **KAMA**: efficiency ratio from a running sum of absolute one-bar changes, clamped to 1; a window whose every
  change is exactly zero (run counter `nullRun`) resets the sum (0.8.x); the smoothing constant is
  `(er*(2/3-2/31) + 2/31)^2` with `fma`; lookback `p + u` (AUTO `100 root`, `200 root`, `root = floor(sqrt p)`); period 1 copies after `u` bars.
- **ZLEMA**: EMA of `2 x[t] - x[t-lag]`, `lag = (p-1)/2`, lookback `lag + p-1 + u`.
- **RMA**: Wilder, seed = mean of `p`, `fma(beta, prev, alpha*x)` with `beta = (p-1)/p`, `alpha = 1-beta`;
  lookback `p-1+u`, AUTO `(10(2p-1)+1)/2`, `(19(2p-1)+1)/2`; period 1 is not special-cased.
- **VIDYA**: EMA with `k = alpha * |CMO|`, CMO over `cmo_period` (2..) changes (the CMOU loop incl. the exact-flat
  reset); lookback `cmo + u`; as an `MaType` the CMO period is `(3p+2)/4`.
- **HMA**: `WMA(2 WMA(x, p/2) - WMA(x, p), floor(sqrt p))`; TA-Lib's fused pass is bit-identical to the
  composition of three TA_WMA runs (their re-anchors included), so the core composes three `WmaCore`s and keeps the
  de-lagged series in a 316-slot ring inside the core (`sqrt(100000)`); lookback `p-1 + s-1`; period 1 copies.
- **ALMA**: Gaussian weights `exp(-(j-m)^2/(2 s^2))/norm`, `m = floor(offset (p-1))`, `s = p/sigma`
  (sigma >= 0.01, offset in [0,1]); the batch function builds the table once (stack up to 64, else `gpa`), the `MaType` and
  the stream recompute each weight (same bits); `exp` is `@exp` (compiler-rt) and agrees with glibc on every compared value.
- **MCGD**: `md += (x-md) / (p (x/md)^4)`, an update that would be non-finite is dropped; period 2..; lookback `p-1+u`.
- **SWAK_BUTTER / SWAK_GAUSS**: two-pole filters, period 2..10000 (not 100000), lookback = the unstable count only
  (AUTO `(13(p+2)+8)/9`, `(22(p+2)+8)/9`), state seeded with the first bar; `sin`/`sqrt` as in the C.
- **MIDPOINT / MIDPRICE / DONCHIAN**: `(highest + lowest)/2` over `p` (2..); DONCHIAN also reports both extremes.
  **ICHIMOKU**: tenkan/kijun/senkou-B midprice windows, senkou-A = `(tenkan+kijun)/2`, no displacement, lookback = longest-1.
- **ACCBANDS**: running sums of `h(1+4(h-l)/(h+l))`, `l(1-...)`, `c`; a bar whose `h+l` is within 1e-14 of its own
  magnitude adds `h`, `l` unwidened; the trailing term is recomputed from the history.
- **KC**: EMA of the typical price `(h+l+c)/3` and ATR (each fed from the bar where its own lookback ends on the
  channel's first bar), `mid +/- ATR*nb_dev`; both take the unstable option.
- **FRAMA**: period even (odd = BadParam), midpoint price, `alpha = exp(-4.6 (D-1))` from the half-window ranges, reset to the price when the
  ranges are degenerate; lookback `p + u` (AUTO `min(9*8(root+2)/2, 990)`, `min(9*12(root+2)/2, 1881)`); the exact window extremes are
  all that matters, so the C's Van Herk slot scheme is replaced by two `ExtCore` pairs (second pair on the half window that ended `p/2` bars ago).
- **VWMA**: `sum(c v)/sum(v)` as `(PV/p)/(V/p)`; a window of exactly zero volume answers NaN (0/0) and resets the sums.
- **MAVP**: per-bar period from a second series, clamped to [min, max] and truncated (NaN gives min), the average of
  that period at that bar, each period run as TA_MA runs it from the first output bar (`startIdx = lookback of max_period`),
  periods 1..10000.
- **SAR / SAREXT**: one state machine (`SarCore(ext)`); the first direction from TA_MINUS_DM with period 1; SAREXT reports the short side negative, supports
  `start_value` and `offset_on_reverse`; lookback 1; accelerations clamp to their maxima as in the C.
- **SUPERTREND**: ATR (the existing `AtrCore`, unstable option) bands around `(h+l)/2` that only tighten while the trend holds; `trend` is `i8` (1 or -1; 0 in the lead);
  period 2.., multiplier [0, 3e37]. **CKSP**: first stops `highest high(p) - m ATR` / `lowest low(p) + m ATR`, then the max / min of the last
  `stop_period` first stops (scratch ring `2 q`); lookback `ATR lookback + q-1`, plus `q-1` more with an AUTO unstable level.
  **ZIGZAG**: percent reversal from bar 0's low, outputs `zigzag` (pivot), `trend` (`i8`), `pivot_idx` (`i32`); lookback = `min_trend_length`.
- **MA with the new types**: every type of `MaType` except MAMA works in MA / MACDEXT / BBANDS / STOCH / STOCHF (period 1 and DISABLED still copy);
  fixed side parameters as TA_MA: T3 vfactor 0.7, VIDYA CMO period `(3p+2)/4`, ALMA sigma 6 offset 0.85. **BBANDS** starts the average at bar 0 and the deviation late
  (TA_BBANDS calls TA_MA with startIdx 0 and realigns): this differs from "feed from the largest lookback" exactly when the average's lookback is
  below the deviation's (VIDYA, found by the oracle; DISABLED copies, so it never showed).

## Limits and refusals

- Periods 1..100000 (2.. where TA-Lib requires it: MAX, MIN, SUM, RSI, MACD fast and slow, BBANDS);
  `Unstable.bars <= 2^30`; BBANDS deviations within ±3e37 (TA-Lib's `TA_REAL_MAX`). Pinned by the
  `BadParam` tests of each file.
- Wave I3 ranges are TA-Lib's: DEMA/TEMA/TRIMA/KAMA/ZLEMA/RMA/HMA/VWMA/VIDYA period 1.., MIDPOINT/MIDPRICE/MCGD/DONCHIAN/ACCBANDS/KC/ICHIMOKU/CKSP/SUPERTREND 2.., SWAK 2..10000,
  MAVP 1..10000 with `min <= max`, T3 vfactor [0,1], ALMA sigma [0.01, 3e37] offset [0,1], SAR/SAREXT parameters [0, 3e37] (start value ±3e37), ZIGZAG sensitivity [0,100], FRAMA even.
- No streaming type for MAVP (a per-bar period needs one average per period: a bank of up to 10000 cores). Streams of CKSP take their scratch in the caller buffer;
  `clone` of a stream re-binds it. CKSP and ALMA batch take an allocator first (CKSP: `2 * stop_period` f64 scratch, ALMA: the weight table above 64 weights).
- `nan = .skip` exists on the recursive functions that never read history (DEMA, TEMA, T3, RMA, MCGD, SWAK, SUPERTREND, KC); not on KAMA / ZLEMA / VIDYA (they read a window, as SMA).
- Integer outputs (SUPERTREND `trend`, ZIGZAG `trend` and `pivot_idx`) are integer slices, 0 in the lead.
- No allocation on the batch path except MACDEXT, STOCH and STOCHF with `f32` input; streaming types that keep a window take a caller buffer and refuse
  a short one with `error.BadParam`. MACDEXT, STOCH and STOCHF keep their intermediate series (MACD line, raw %K, slow %K) in f64: with `f64` the output slices double as that scratch and nothing is allocated; with `f32` they allocate `n` (MACDEXT, STOCHF) or `2n` (STOCH) f64 from the `gpa` argument and free it before returning (`error.OutOfMemory`).
- Deliberate differences from TA-Lib: per-call unstable period instead of a process-global one;
  RSI answers NaN (not 50) when its internal state is NaN: TA-Lib tests `gain + loss > 0` and a NaN
  fails that test, so a poisoned RSI would read as the neutral 50, which looks like a valid
  reading, while NaN says "no value" (batch and stream agree). `nan = .skip` exists only here: a NaN
  bar leaves the state untouched and the OUTPUT at that bar carries the previous output (NaN while
  there is none), like pandas `ewm(ignore_na=True)`; the bar does not count towards the lookback.
  For `f32` input all intermediate series are f64 (as in TA-Lib's `TA_S_*`) and the result is
  rounded once on writing `out` (tested: f32 output == `@floatCast` of the f64 output for the
  f32-rounded input).

## Anchoring

**External anchor, live:** `tools/interop.zig` drives TA-Lib C 0.8.3 (our own compile of its audited
sources into a static archive, behind the C shim `tools/talib_oracle.c`; `zig build interop-indicators`)
over 5751 records: every seed and wave-I3 function, f64 input (`TA_<F>`) and f32 input (`TA_S_<F>`), seeded
random-walk OHLC inputs (also flat-run and 1e-9-scaled kinds), a parameter grid with defaults, edges,
swapped fast/slow, every `MaType` but MAMA in every MA slot and out-of-range values, the unstable period at
0, 3, AUTO4 and AUTO8 (`TA_SetUnstablePeriod`), and lengths 1, 2, period-1, period, period+1,
lookback..lookback+2, 40, 300 and (first parameter set) 5000; VWMA and MAVP get a second generated series (volume with zero stretches; periods -1..15 with NaN), the integer outputs travel as doubles. It compares the return code (BadParam
against `TA_BAD_PARAM`), the lookback against `TA_<F>_Lookback`, `outBegIdx == lookback` and
`outNBElement == n - lookback`, the NaN lead, and every value. **Result (2026-11-15): all 1.5 million
compared values are bitwise equal (the seed alone 1.5 million, wave I3 another 0.9 million), the per-function ULP bound is 0 for every function incl. ALMA / FRAMA / SWAK (`exp`, `log`, `sin` from compiler-rt agree with the oracle's libm on every sampled input; not a guarantee for all inputs)** (TA-Lib 0.8.3,
x86-64, our `cc` line). One disagreement was found on the first run and it was ours: `MACDFIX` built its
0.15/0.075 pair from untyped float literals, which Zig folds at more than double precision, so
`1 - (1 - 0.15)` differed from TA-Lib's double-by-double value by up to 6e7 ULP; fixed (typed `f64`
constants), pinned by the oracle. Wave I3 brought one more, also ours (not TA-Lib's): BBANDS fed its moving average from the largest lookback, TA-Lib starts it at bar 0; the two agree unless the average's lookback is below the deviation's, which VIDYA is (see the BBANDS note). The oracle found no defect in TA-Lib, so there is no "lead" to record.

**External anchor, frozen:** `src/testdata/talib_vectors.zig` holds 294 of those records (n = 40, the
first parameter sets of each function, one f32 record per function, AUTO4 and bars unstable) as bit
patterns of TA-Lib's answers; `src/oracle_test.zig` replays them in the ordinary test lane. Regenerate
with `zig build interop-indicators -- --emit-vectors modules/indicators/src/testdata/talib_vectors.zig`, then `zig fmt` it.

Not covered by the oracle: `nan = .skip` and `seed = .first` (options TA-Lib does not have; tested against
our own batch/stream definitions), the windowed functions with NaN input (TA-Lib's own behaviour is
unspecified; pinned by tests), MAMA, parameters beyond the grid, optimised modes, other libm implementations.

**Anchor grade:** class B · oracle EXTERNAL

## What is deliberately not done

- Not now: the other 196 functions; MAMA and HT_TRENDLINE (Cycle wave; `ma` answers `error.Unsupported` for MAMA);
  candlesticks; math transform / vector arithmetic groups; `nan = .skip` on the windowed indicators; a streaming MAVP.
- Not now: SIMD fast paths, benchmark against TA-Lib and `kand` (wave I4).
- Never: process-global configuration (unstable period, candle settings) — options are per call.

## Open

- Bitwise agreement with TA-Lib is measured for one toolchain (x86-64, the coordinator's `cc` line); a
  TA-Lib compiled with a different contraction policy could differ by an ULP where its C spells
  `a*b - c*d` (BBANDS/VAR variance); we never contract. Re-run the oracle on aarch64 before claiming it there.
- NaN semantics of the windowed indicators (SMA, WMA, SUM, BBANDS, STOCH): a NaN enters the running
  sums and stays there until a re-anchor (WMA every 8p outputs, the variance every 32 windows)
  rebuilds them; pinned by tests, equal to TA-Lib's C by reading, not by running. MAX/MIN: a NaN never
  wins a comparison and only shows when it opens a rescan; ties keep the OLDEST value on a rescan
  (`>` / `<`) and the NEWEST on an incremental update (`>=` / `<=`), so 0.0 vs -0.0 follows that
  rule (pinned).

## Backlog / deferred

- MAMA (period ignored, lookback 32): wire into `MaCore` with the Cycle wave.
- A streaming MAVP (bank of averages, caller buffer).
- In-place calls (`out` aliasing `in`): TA-Lib allows them, the batch functions here do not.
- Streaming for the windowed indicators with a ring that is shared between components of one composite
  (BBANDS keeps two rings of the same window for SMA).
